name: El Guapo
label: Dischord
lede: Justin Moyer and Rafael Cohen started a band with an accordion and an oboe, made a Dischord record in a Philadelphia living room, then found a Chicago band with beer-commercial backing already owned the name.

eras.title: Two students and a pile of instruments
eras.text: Justin Moyer and Rafael Cohen started El Guapo with instruments nobody else in DC was plugging in. Through the late '90s the line-up shifted and the records came out on Resin and on the band's own Mud Memory, a long way from the Dischord house.

years.h: El Guapo starts as a duo, at Wesleyan or in DC
years.p: Wikipedia has [[Justin Moyer|68cb15fd-5c0c-4b60-ad06-935ac0756a4d]] and [[Rafael Cohen|346eee0b-4f6d-48e3-a454-ca69846a845a]] forming the band at Wesleyan University. Dischord's bio says it began in Washington, DC, in 1996, as two people.
years.xp:
Moyer, born in Philadelphia in 1977, handled vocals, bass, drums and electronics. Cohen played guitar and, eventually, oboe, an instrument you don't often find on a punk label's roster.

The line-up kept changing for the rest of the decade, with [[Pete Cafarella|8b976a27-0459-4c70-b6e6-6ef0277a254f]] arriving on accordion and keyboards and [[Nate Smith|b6b7fe2f-e015-4820-9577-77aa93f319a9]] on drums.

years.h: An untitled 7" on Red Skies at Night is El Guapo's first record
years.p: Dischord's catalog lists the four songs as 4 Songs.

years.h: The Burden of History arrives on Resin
years.p: El Guapo's first full-length comes out on D.C.'s Resin label, with a title that reaches for grand abstractions.

years.h: A second Resin album, The Phenomenon of Renewal
years.p: The line-up Wikipedia lists has Smith on drums.

years.h: The Geography of Dissolution goes out on the band's own label
years.p: A CD of improvised live pieces on Mud Memory, the last El Guapo record before Dischord.

years.h: Smith leaves the drums and three people carry on
years.p: Smith goes before the band signs to Dischord, per Wikipedia. Moyer, Cohen and Cafarella split the drums, bass and electronics among them.

eras.title: The Pet Sounds of DC postpunk
eras.text: On Dischord, El Guapo made oboe-and-accordion pop over drum machines on Super/System. They toured hard, and Fake French, cut mostly at Moyer's parents' house, became their best seller.

years.h: Super/System lands at Dischord No. 128
years.p: Recorded in March 2001 with Phil Manley of [[Trans Am|7c5acaaa-3f74-4e16-82b2-f8046fce4338]] at National Recording Studio: eighteen tracks in forty-two minutes. Dischord quotes People magazine calling it the Pet Sounds of D.C. postpunk.
years.xp:
[[Chad Clark|f3f09e99-e31c-4aa2-99e4-0b4e59e72f87]] mastered it at Silver Sonya. The tracks run from My Bird Sings to Being Boulevards.

It was a three-piece by now, each member credited with vocals and electronics on top of a main instrument: Moyer on bass and drums, Cohen on guitar and oboe, Cafarella on accordion.

years.h: More than 100 shows across the US and Europe in a single year
years.p: According to the band's bio, El Guapo keeps that pace through 2003 and 2004 too.

yt: Ocean and Sky, from Fake French
years.h: Fake French is cut in Moyer's parents' living room
years.p: The bio says the album was recorded mostly at the Moyer family house outside Philadelphia and mixed by Chad Clark at Inner Ear. Dischord (No. 134) calls it El Guapo's bestselling release on the label.
years.xp:
The self-recording stretched across sessions over six months. Twelve songs this time, tighter and more danceable, with titles like Space Tourist and Hollywood Crew.

One track is called Justin Destroyer, and the name stuck: Moyer is billed as Justin Destroyer in Supersystem.

years.h: Live at Contrappunto, Perugia, Italy, November 2, 2003
yt: Live at Contrappunto, Perugia, Italy, November 2, 2003

eras.title: A Chicago band keeps the name
eras.text: Drummer Josh Blair arrived, Touch and Go called, and a Chicago band with corporate backing turned out to own the name El Guapo. The DC band became Supersystem, made two records for Touch and Go, and broke up in November 2006.

years.cap: Supersystem at Sala Rossa, Montreal, January 2006
years.h: Josh Blair arrives from Orthrelm
years.p: With Blair, a drummer out of [[Orthrelm|34b67ccb-3bcb-49a4-8109-1c5282b1e0a0]]'s hyper-technical instrumental attack, El Guapo is a four-piece for the first time since Smith left.

q: You can bet that we're looking into trademarking 'Supersystem.'
years.h: El Guapo becomes Supersystem, and a Chicago band keeps the name
years.p: Cohen on the old name, to Washington City Paper. He said Touch and Go "kinda suggested" the change when the band moved to the label.
years.xp:
A Chicago group also called El Guapo had filed for a trademark on live performances in April 2002, with frontman Michael Lopez listed as owner that October. The band had corporate backing, including McDonald's and Budweiser commercials. Cohen: "It seemed like if they had those kinds of people behind them, then they would have the kind of muscle to take us on." He even suggested the Chicago band play the HFStival.

Wikipedia tells a softer version: a new drummer, and a general dislike of the original name. Cohen also cited Touch and Go's co-op advertising and its distribution through Warner's ADA.

years.h: Supersystem's first record for Touch and Go, Always Never Again
years.p: Touch and Go pitches the band as a NY/DC quartet mixing hip-hop, electronica, punk and world music, with Moyer now billed as Justin Destroyer.

years.cap: Supersystem at the Black Cat, Washington, DC, January 7, 2006
years.h: Supersystem plays home turf at the Black Cat
years.p: A January night at D.C.'s Black Cat, the show behind the photo Wikipedia runs for the band.

years.h: A Million Microphones is the last Supersystem record
years.p: Touch and Go puts out the band's second and final album.

years.cap: Supersystem at the Touch and Go 25th Anniversary, Chicago, September 2006
yt: Touch and Go 25th Anniversary set, Hideout
years.h: Supersystem breaks up ten years after the duo began
years.p: The band calls it quits in November, a couple of months after playing Touch and Go's 25th anniversary weekend in Chicago.

eras.title: Scattered across the dance floor
eras.text: Cohen went to the dance-punk band !!!, Cafarella to synth-pop, and Moyer, after a solo act that started in drag, to the Washington Post newsroom. The El Guapo records went up on Bandcamp and stayed in the Dischord catalog.

years.cap: Pete Cafarella on keyboards with Supersystem, Touch and Go 25th Anniversary, Chicago, September 2006
years.h: Cohen joins !!!, Cafarella and Smith start Shy Child
years.p: Cohen takes a spot in !!!. Cafarella and Smith reunite as the synth-pop duo [[Shy Child|78357d35-1c85-41c3-b134-37dbca97dd65]], and Blair goes back to Orthrelm.

years.h: Moyer takes a desk at the Washington Post
years.p: Alongside [[Edie Sedgwick|63b1219b-1910-4dfc-8ea5-6df6b2e7ac75]], his solo project that first performed in drag to iPod backing, Moyer starts writing for the Post on books, poker and city politics.

years.h: Moyer's trio [[Light Beams|42b3e741-bdf8-402e-acdf-f73c2a491951]] wins a WAMMIE
years.p: The Washington Area Music Association award is for Self Help.

years.h: Moyer is on the Post team that wins a Pulitzer
years.p: The paper's coverage of the January 6 Capitol attack wins the prize, and Wikipedia lists Moyer on the team.
